text: Applying the structure theorem for finitely generated modules over a PID with R = F[x], acting on V through a linear operator T, yields:
choices: the rational canonical form of T (and Jordan form when F is algebraically closed)
the singular value decomposition of T
the characteristic polynomial as a product of quadratics
explanation: V ≅ ⊕ F[x]/(fᵢ) with f₁ | f₂ | ⋯ gives the invariant factors, i.e. companion-matrix blocks (RCF); the primary decomposition over an algebraically closed field gives Jordan blocks. With R = ℤ the same theorem classifies finitely generated abelian groups.
